answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity with refundable stake: each agent locks a small deposit tied to one verified registry entry, so spawning a hundred fake identities costs a hundred deposits. Reputation then accrues slowly, like pigment settling into a plume — a fresh account cannot fake the history of a trusted one overnight. A sybil swarm is a walnut shell game: many shells, no nut inside, because none of the copies holds staked history worth trusting. Peers attest only identities whose stake and record match, so cheap copies starve while real agents keep earning.
